knowledge:
- key_parameters: sequencing_data=Logical (default TRUE); set to FALSE if expression data are from microarrays rather than sequencing ;; normalize=Logical (default TRUE); automatically normalizes expression data ;; interactions=Custom interaction data frame; if NULL, the package automatically retrieves interactions from databases like OmnipathR or TransmiR ;; type=Character ("tf", "miRNA_target", "tf_miRNA") used in run_tf_integration to specify the regulator-target relationship type for automatic database download ;; data=A MultiAssayExperiment object containing the multi-omics datasets for run_multiomics ;; omics=Character string (e.g., "gene_genomic_res") specifying the omics model results to plot ;; cnv_met=Character string ("cnv" or "met") specifying the genomic modification type for plotting
- alternatives: None mentioned
- when_to_use: Use when you have matched multi-omics data (gene expression, miRNA expression, methylation, and/or CNV) for the same set of samples and want to model how genomic modifications and transcriptional regulators collectively influence gene or miRNA expression.
- pitfalls: Customizing genomic interactions by linking multiple covariates to a single response may make the output incompatible with the Shiny visualization app ;; Only the output of the run_multiomics function is compatible with run_shiny ;; Input matrices for individual two-omics integration functions (run_genomic_integration, run_cnv_integration, etc.) must have samples as rows and features as columns, requiring transposition (t()) of standard Bioconductor expression matrices.

workflows.name: two_omics_integration
workflows.intent: Integrate gene or miRNA expression data with a single genomic modification (CNV or methylation) or transcriptional regulator (TF or miRNA) using individual matrices.
input: gene_exp_matrix.csv (Gene expression matrix with genes as rows and samples as columns)
cnv_matrix.csv (Copy number variation matrix with genes as rows and samples as columns)
meth_matrix.csv (Methylation matrix with genes as rows and samples as columns)
miRNA_exp_matrix.csv (miRNA expression matrix with miRNAs as rows and samples as columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Transpose input matrices so that samples are represented as rows and features as columns ;; 2. Run the specific integration function (run_genomic_integration, run_cnv_integration, run_met_integration, or run_tf_integration) ;; 3. Summarize the integration model results using summary.
workflows.code:
gene_genomic_integration <- run_genomic_integration(expression = t(gene_exp_matrix),
                                                    cnv_data = t(gene_cnv_matrix),
                                                    methylation = t(meth_matrix))
summary(gene_genomic_integration)

gene_cnv_integration <- run_cnv_integration(expression = t(gene_exp_matrix),
                                            cnv_data = t(gene_cnv_matrix))
summary(gene_cnv_integration)

gene_met_integration <- run_met_integration(expression = t(gene_exp_matrix),
                                            methylation = t(meth_matrix))
summary(gene_met_integration)

tf_target_integration <- run_tf_integration(expression = t(gene_exp_matrix),
                                            type = "tf")
summary(tf_target_integration)

miRNA_target_integration <- run_tf_integration(expression = t(gene_exp_matrix),
                                               tf_expression = t(miRNA_exp_matrix),
                                               type = "miRNA_target")
summary(miRNA_target_integration)

tf_miRNA_integration <- run_tf_integration(expression = t(miRNA_exp_matrix),
                                               tf_expression = t(gene_exp_matrix),
                                               type = "tf_miRNA")
summary(tf_miRNA_integration)

workflows.name: complete_multiomics_integration
workflows.intent: Perform a complete multi-omics integration using a MultiAssayExperiment, followed by downstream interactive visualization, static plotting, and functional enrichment analysis.
input: gene_exp_matrix.csv (Gene expression matrix with genes as rows and samples as columns)
miRNA_exp_matrix.csv (miRNA expression matrix with miRNAs as rows and samples as columns)
meth_matrix.csv (Methylation matrix with genes as rows and samples as columns)
gene_cnv_matrix.csv (Gene CNV matrix with genes as rows and samples as columns)
miRNA_cnv_matrix.csv (miRNA CNV matrix with miRNAs as rows and samples as columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Create a MultiAssayExperiment object using create_multiassay ;; 2. Run the complete multi-omics integration using run_multiomics ;; 3. Extract model results using extract_model_res ;; 4. Launch the interactive Shiny visualization app using run_shiny ;; 5. Generate static plots (network, Venn, volcano, ridge, chromosome distribution, TF distribution) ;; 6. Run genomic enrichment using run_genomic_enrich and visualize with dot_plotly.
workflows.code:
new_multiassay <- create_multiassay(methylation = meth_matrix, 
                                    gene_exp = gene_exp_matrix,
                                    cnv_data = gene_cnv_matrix,
                                    miRNA_exp = miRNA_exp_matrix,
                                    miRNA_cnv_data = miRNA_cnv_matrix)

multiomics_integration <- run_multiomics(data = new_multiassay)
summary(multiomics_integration)

run_shiny(multiomics_integration)

data_table <- extract_model_res(multiomics_integration)
data_table <- data_table[data_table$cov!="(Intercept)",]
